label: No
summary: The value false, written `no`.
details: Used where a yes/no value is needed, for example `is_adult = no`. It works anywhere, in any scope.

label: Noble family title
summary: The noble family title of the dynasty house.
details: Starts from a dynasty house and leads to a title. Vanilla uses it a few times.

label: Obedience target
summary: The character's obedience target, another character.
details: Starts from a character and leads to another character. The game does not explain what the obedience is, only that vanilla uses it often.

label: Contract obligation
summary: The obligation level of a vassal contract, picked by its key.
details: Written `obligation:<key>` on a vassal contract. The game's documentation calls the key a decision type, which looks like a copy-paste error, and vanilla never uses this link, so the exact key is not confirmed.

label: Order faith
summary: The faith of the holy order.
details: Starts from a holy order and leads to its faith. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Order founder
summary: The character who founded the holy order.
details: Only works if a founder was given when the order was created; otherwise there is nothing to lead to. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Order founding rite
summary: The founding tenet of the holy order, as a rite.
details: The game's documentation says the result might be invalid, so check that it exists before using it. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Order tenet
summary: The tenet of the holy order.
details: Starts from a holy order and leads to a tenet. Vanilla uses it often.

label: Organization
summary: The organization of a character or a faith.
details: Works from a character or from a faith.

label: Origin faith
summary: Starts from a faith and leads to another faith; going by its name, the faith it originated from.
details: The game's documentation text is a copy of the religion link's doc (it talks about religion), so it does not describe this link. The meaning here rests on the name only, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Origin rite
summary: The origin rite of the rite.
details: Starts from a rite and leads to another rite. The game documents nothing more, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Outbreak province
summary: The province where the epidemic outbreak started.
details: Starts from an epidemic and leads to a province. Vanilla uses it often.

label: Overlord
summary: The character's overlord, meaning their suzerain or their liege.
details: Starts from a character and leads to another character. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Domicile owner
summary: The character who owns the domicile.
details: Starts from a domicile and leads to its owner. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Group's situation
summary: The situation that the situation participant group belongs to.

label: Group's sub-region
summary: The situation sub-region that the situation participant group belongs to.

label: Player heir
summary: The character's player heir.
details: Starts from a character and leads to another character. The game does not say what makes an heir a player heir, only that vanilla uses it a lot.

label: Assumed father of the baby
summary: The character who is assumed to be the father of the character's unborn baby.
details: Starts from the character carrying the baby. The game's documentation names the real father as a separate link, `pregnancy_real_father`.

label: Real father of the baby
summary: The real father of the character's unborn baby.
details: Starts from the character carrying the baby. The assumed father is a separate link, `pregnancy_assumed_father`.

label: Previous scope
summary: The thing that the script was looking at just before the current one.
details: Works everywhere. After stepping into something (a list or a link), `prev` goes back one step. Vanilla uses it a lot.

label: Previous holder
summary: The character who held the title before its current holder.
details: Starts from a title and leads to a character.

label: Previous owner
summary: The previous owner of the artifact.
details: The game's documentation says "activity", but the link starts from an artifact, so that word looks like a copy-paste error. It leads to a character.

label: Owner before the previous
summary: The owner of the artifact two owners ago.
details: One step further back than `previous_owner`. The game's documentation says "activity", but the link starts from an artifact, so that looks like a copy-paste error.

label: Owner three owners ago
summary: The owner of the artifact three owners ago.
details: One step further back than `previous_owner_level_2`. The game's documentation says "activity", but the link starts from an artifact, so that looks like a copy-paste error.

label: Primary attacker
summary: The main attacker of the war or casus belli (the reason for war).
details: Leads to a character. Vanilla uses it often.

label: Primary defender
summary: The main defender of the war or casus belli (the reason for war).
details: Leads to a character. Vanilla uses it often.

label: Primary heir
summary: The character's primary heir.
details: Starts from a character and leads to another character.

label: Primary partner
summary: The character's primary partner, such as a spouse or a consort.
details: Starts from a character and leads to another character.

label: Primary spouse
summary: The character's primary spouse.
details: Starts from a character and leads to another character. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Primary title
summary: The character's primary title.
details: Starts from a character and leads to a title. It is one of the most used links in vanilla.

label: Promoted legend
summary: The legend that the character promotes.
details: Starts from a character and leads to a legend.

label: Province by ID
summary: A specific province, picked by its ID number.
details: Written `province:<id>`. It works anywhere. Vanilla uses it once.

label: Province owner
summary: The character who owns the province.
details: Starts from a province and leads to a character.

label: Puppet of a type
summary: The character's puppet of the given type.
details: Written `puppet:<type>`, for example `character.puppet:clerical_puppet`. The game's documentation says it gives a result only if it applies and the puppet is compliant; it does not explain what compliant means.

label: Puppeteer
summary: The character's puppeteer.
details: The game's documentation says it gives a result only if it applies and the character is compliant; it does not explain what compliant means.

label: Real father
summary: The character's real father.
details: Starts from a character and leads to another character. Vanilla uses it a fair amount.

label: Real mother
summary: The character's real mother.
details: Vanilla does not use it.

label: Realm priest
summary: The realm priest of the character.
details: Starts from a character and leads to another character. Vanilla uses it only twice.

label: Regiment controller
summary: The character who currently controls the regiment.
details: Vanilla does not use it.

label: Regiment's controlling title
summary: A title of the regiment; the game's documentation calls it the owning title, going by its name the title that controls it.
details: The game's documentation repeats the text of `regiment_owning_title` ("owning title"), so how this differs from it is not stated.

label: Regiment owner
summary: The character who owns the regiment.

label: Regiment's owning title
summary: The title that owns the regiment.

label: Regiment station
summary: The province where the regiment is stationed.
details: Vanilla does not use it.

label: Religion
summary: The religion of a character, title, province, faith, great holy war or rite.
details: Vanilla uses this very often.

label: Religion by key
summary: A specific religion, picked by its key.
details: Written `religion:<key>`. It works anywhere. Vanilla uses it very often (the count in the input is shared with the other `religion` link).

label: Head of faith
summary: The character who is the religious head of the faith.
details: Starts from a faith and leads to a character. Vanilla uses it often.

label: Head of faith or challenger
summary: The challenger the character follows, or the head of their faith if they follow none.
details: The result can be empty (null), so check it exists before using it.

label: Title of the head of faith
summary: The title held by the religious head of the faith.
details: Starts from a faith and leads to a title.

label: Rite
summary: The rite of a character, title or province.
details: Vanilla uses it very often (the count in the input is shared with the other `rite` link).

label: Rite by key
summary: A specific rite, picked by its key.
details: Written `rite:<key>`. It works anywhere.
